data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'hagos' meaning 'farmer' or 'soil'. In the New Testament, St. Hippolytus of Rome is known as 'Hagios Hippolytos' meaning 'Holy Hippolytus'. The name Hock carries the meaning “Farmer” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Hock usually hope their child will grow to embody farmer and live with faith, good character and purpose.

Hock may symbolize a connection to Christian tradition and history, representing a deep rooted commitment to the faith.

Hock embodies the virtues of faith, perseverance, and scholarship, as St. Hippolytus was not only a martyr but also a renowned scholar and theologian. Thus, the name holds a deep spiritual significance, representing not only a connection to the Christian community but also a commitment to seeking knowledge and understanding of the divine.
